How CrossnoKaye grounds physical AI with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
CrossnoKaye took a different approach to bring physical AI to heavy industry using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore .

To back every numerical answer with real math, AURA uses the code interpreter capability in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to write and run Python workloads at runtime inside isolated, AWS managed microVM sandboxes, alongside Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and local edge safety controls.

This post covers how CrossnoKaye architected ATLAS and AURA on AWS, how AURA uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore across interactive Chats, repeatable Tasks, and automated Routines, and what the team learned running physical AI in production.
Figure 1: CrossnoKaye AURA and ATLAS physical AI architecture with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

In the cloud, CrossnoKaye’s Scheduling system runs two continuous pipelines from versioned Python packages in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) , operating on configurable per-instance cadences and event-driven triggers when plant settings change.

Isolated Python execution: The Sandbox Orchestrator uses the AWS SDK to call the endpoint for the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, staging datasets and running model-authored Python inside an isolated code interpreter microVM.
